_comment: Ujwal's fixture. ONE shared file: Soham builds his fake /ask branch from this, and web/index.html reads it. Frozen contract, all values real, from Bhushan's GROUND_TRUTH.md. Do not fork it - if you change the shape, change it here and tell both consumers.

contract.response: SSE stream of { answer, trail[], stale[] }
contract.native_eventsource_warning: POST means EventSource will NOT work. Use fetch() + response.body.getReader(). A stuck spinner at Gate 2 is this bug, not a server bug.

shape_notes.answer: Array of short strings. The frontend concatenates and renders one per tick, so a streamer can be tested against real content. Backend may stream a single string; join it.
shape_notes.trail: Ordered chain, index 0 first. Each row carries the edge label that linked it to the PREVIOUS row.
shape_notes.trail[].type: Chip label / badge. One of: Person, Decision, Document, Message, Service, Project, Team.
shape_notes.trail[].name: Main chip text.
shape_notes.trail[].detail: Secondary text. Expands when the chip is clicked to show the raw sub-result.
shape_notes.trail[].date: Secondary text on the chip. Present on EVERY row. May be empty string where the fact has no date (e.g. blast radius) - empty is a value, missing the key is a bug.
shape_notes.trail[].via_edge: The edge label drawn between this chip and the previous one. NEVER dropped - without it the trail is a list of things that happened to be near each other instead of a proof chain.
shape_notes.stale: Renders as a warning badge on the matching chip. Match by (type, name), not by index.
shape_notes.stale[].name: Must exactly match a trail[] name to badge it. If it does not match anything, it renders as a standalone warning line - which is correct, not a failure.
shape_notes.stale[].reason: Why it is stale. Shown in the badge tooltip.
shape_notes.stale[].last_verified_at: Date the staleness was established. Drives the badge tooltip.

demo.question: Who knows about the payments service, what breaks if it goes down, and where was that decided?
answer: Ravi Menon is the right person to ask about payments right now.
He has owned payments-gateway since 2026-04-15, when ownership moved
from Priya Sharma.
Priya Sharma still has the most commits on it (14),
but her last touch was 2026-04-15 and she left the company that day,
so she is not a current answer.
The migration was decided in D-14 on 2026-03-18,
which has since been superseded by D-19 on 2026-05-06:
dual provider, Adyen primary.
If payments-gateway goes down, 8 services break across 3 hops.
The evaluation doc payments-provider-eval-v3.md still says Stripe-only
and is out of date - follow D-19, not the doc.

failure.question: Who owns config-service?
answer: Nobody - that is a real answer, not a gap in the data.
config-service has no :OWNED_BY edge in the graph.
There is no team and no person attached to it.
Mei Lin is the most recent contributor to it and is a reasonable person to ask
about it, but she does not own it.
I won't name an owner, because none exists in the graph.

stale_ranking.is_demo_beat: beat 3 - the trap. The naive ORDER BY commits DESC answer is Priya and it is the WRONG answer. Do not flatten this tension.
stale_ranking.question: Who should I ask about the payments service?
answer: Ravi Menon.
But the reason matters, so here is the tension rather than a clean answer.
Priya Sharma has the most commits on payments-migration - 14 of them.
By volume alone she is the top contributor.
Her last touch was 2026-04-15 and she left the company on that date,
so that volume is history, not current knowledge.
Ravi Menon took ownership on 2026-04-15 and is still active on the project.
Ana Duarte is worth a second opinion if the question touches ledger:
she is the only person who has worked on both payments and ledger.
So: most commits = Priya. Best person to ask now = Ravi.

blast_radius.is_demo_beat: beat 2 supporting - what breaks, and who gets paged.
blast_radius.question: What breaks if payments-gateway dies?
answer: 8 services break, across 3 hops.
Directly: checkout-api, config-service, dispute-service, mobile-bff, notifications, webhook-relay.
One hop further out: fraud-scoring.
Two hops: recommendation.
Ownership is split - checkout-api, mobile-bff and dispute-service sit with Payments,
notifications and recommendation with Growth, fraud-scoring with Risk.
config-service has no team at all, so there is nobody to page for it.
ledger-core and settlement-batch do NOT break - they are upstream of payments-gateway.
One risk: notifications has had no contributor touch since 2026-05-02,
so its owner may not be able to respond quickly.

trail.name: config-service
trail.detail: depth 1 - NO owner and NO team. Nothing to page.

trail.name: notifications
trail.detail: depth 1 - owned by team Growth. No contributor since 2026-05-02 - bus-factor risk.

trail.name: fraud-scoring
trail.detail: depth 2 - owned by team Risk (Diego Alvarez)

stale.reason: No contributor touch since 2026-05-02, over 90 days stale. One hop from payments-gateway.

excluded_upstream._note: Deliberately NOT in blast_radius. These depend on ledger-core, which is upstream of payments-gateway. If your query returns these, your edge direction is inverted.
